tool.name: CumulativeSurface

summary.para: Combines any mix of polygon layers and rasters into one integer raster whose cell value counts how many of those layers occur on that cell -- a way of estimating the relative importance (or the number of species served) of preserving that ground. Built to combine patch polygon maps and corridor rasters across species, but combines any polygon/raster mix. Each layer counts at most once per cell no matter how many of its polygons overlap there. Needs no Spatial Analyst.

tool.usage:
What counts as "present". A raster counts on a cell when its value there is neither NoData nor zero -- a corridor raster's 0 background never counts, exactly as the original tool ran every raster through SetNull(value = 0) first. Keep that rule in mind when combining arbitrary rasters whose 0 is meaningful data. A polygon layer counts where any of its (optionally: selected) polygons covers the cell center, the same test Polygon To Raster uses -- and it counts once there even where several of its polygons overlap each other. That layer-level counting is the difference from Esri's Count Overlapping Features, which counts overlapping features: here two overlapping patches of the same species still mean one species served.
Selections. With "Use only selected polygons" checked, each polygon map layer's active selection is honored independently; a layer with no selection (or an empty one) contributes all its polygons -- the original tool's documented fallback. Selection state exists only on map layers: a dataset picked with the Browse button always contributes every polygon.
The shared grid. Every raster input must be in one coordinate system -- the tool refuses otherwise, because resampling presence between projections would silently shift it. Polygon layers may be in any known coordinate system; they are projected on the fly (true-curve polygons are densified first so geodatabase circles and arcs rasterize correctly). The output uses the first raster's coordinate system (or the first layer's when no rasters are given), a cell size equal to the smallest cell size among the input rasters (or 1/1000 of the longest extent edge when all inputs are polygons -- both overridable with the cell size parameter), and the union of every input's extent. The grid is snapped to the smallest-cell raster's own cell origin so raster presence never shifts by a fraction of a cell.
The output is a small integer raster (Byte where the layer count allows) with a value attribute table (Value / Count / Class_Name) and a legend ready to draw: 0 in white, then the color-blind-friendly viridis ramp -- dark violet (fewest layers) through teal to bright yellow (most). (The original shaded red through yellow to green; that red-green pairing is the classic color-blindness confusion, so this version uses viridis instead.) The optional legend label word is appended to each class, so with "Species" the legend reads "0 Species", "1 Species", "2 Species", ... Optionally cells where no layer occurs are written as NoData instead of the white 0 class -- useful when the empty background would hide layers underneath. Layer transparency, which the original offered as a convenience, is set in Pro on the Raster Layer ribbon or Layer Properties.
Provenance. The output carries full metadata plus a machine-readable linkage record listing every source layer (with its selection state and any analysis identifiers found); the Corridor Analysis Data Report window reads it back, appending each record-carrying source's own analysis history. Combining sources from different analyses -- one corridor per species -- is the tool's normal use, and the report says so rather than warning.
A modernized port of the CorridorDesigner Evaluation Tools' Cumulative Surface Tool. Needs no Spatial Analyst license.

param.name: datasets
param.displayname: Layers to combine (polygon layers and rasters)

dialogReference.para: Any mix of polygon feature layers/classes and rasters. Select several layers in the Contents pane and drag them all into this list at once, or browse and multi-select datasets from disk. Every raster must share one coordinate system; polygon layers may be in any known coordinate system.

The output integer raster: each cell counts how many input layers occur there (0 up to the number of layers). Written with a value attribute table (Value / Count / Class_Name) and symbolized with the color-blind-friendly viridis ramp -- dark violet (fewest) through teal to bright yellow (most), 0 in white. A folder destination gets a GeoTIFF; a geodatabase gets a native raster.

param.name: per_feature
param.displayname: Treat each polygon as a separate layer (a cell counts the polygons covering it)

dialogReference.para: Checked: every polygon feature counts as its own layer, so a cell's value is the number of polygons covering it. This is how one feature class holding a corridor per land facet (or per species) is combined without exporting each corridor separately: select the slices you want and check this box. A multipart feature counts once; several single-part features that overlap each count, so dissolve a strand stored as separate parts first if that is not what you want. Rasters still count once each. Unchecked (default): a polygon layer counts once wherever any of its polygons lies, however many overlap. In both modes each polygon map layer's active selection is honored (an empty selection means all its polygons); use the Use the selected records switch Pro shows under each layer.

A word appended to every legend class. With "Species" the legend reads "0 Species", "1 Species", "2 Species", ... Stored in the raster's Class_Name attribute field, so the labels survive into any map legend.

param.name: zero_to_nodata
param.displayname: Exclude areas where no layers occur (0 becomes NoData)

dialogReference.para: Checked: cells where no input layer occurs are written as NoData, so the empty background disappears and layers underneath show through. Unchecked (default): those cells hold 0 and draw white.

Overrides the automatic cell size, in the output coordinate system's linear units. Left blank: the smallest cell size among the input rasters, or -- when every input is a polygon layer -- 1/1000 of the longest edge of the combined extent (the original tool's rules).

scriptExample.title: Cumulative Surface example (stand-alone script)
scriptExample.para: Count how many species' corridor footprints cover each cell.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path arcpy.jenness.CumulativeSurface( datasets=[r"D:\data\linkages.gdb\blackbear_corridor", r"D:\data\linkages.gdb\cwtdeer_corridor", r"D:\data\linkages.gdb\coati_patches"], out_raster=r"D:\data\linkages.gdb\species_served", per_feature=False, legend_label="Species", zero_to_nodata=True)
